### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/hono`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5f84ef0ecad1c2ca82e2874fe5540a22cb35b954`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5f84ef0ecad1c2ca82e2874fe5540a22cb35b954` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `45ec92c7151a418981019e2004bfecacd3c998db` — the merge of head `06bca6c55126385ae1b54d3b0a516cf3e15ae16a` into base `5f84ef0ecad1c2ca82e2874fe5540a22cb35b954`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 45ec92c7151a418981019e2004bfecacd3c998db && git checkout 45ec92c7151a418981019e2004bfecacd3c998db
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5f84ef0ecad1c2ca82e2874fe5540a22cb35b954 06bca6c55126385ae1b54d3b0a516cf3e15ae16a && git checkout -B drift-repro 5f84ef0ecad1c2ca82e2874fe5540a22cb35b954 && git merge --no-ff 06bca6c55126385ae1b54d3b0a516cf3e15ae16a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5f84ef0ecad1c2ca82e2874fe5540a22cb35b954
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5f84ef0ecad1c2ca82e2874fe5540a22cb35b954` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Verdict: FAIL
Head-sha: `a517fa2e` `a517fa2e188d4f2f0222658f4f1324b211142967`
Reviewer tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER (independent of the author)
Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts, the `Clause-②: yes` declaration (PR body, changeset) + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, auth-manager.ts, one-time-token-handoff.ts, sys-session-revoke.ts, auth-route-ledger.ts, auth-handle-request-surface.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json, packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/auth.ts, the two peer-pin tests, .changeset/auth-handlerequest-whole-surface.md

**One must-fix, and it is a declaration, not code: the diff narrows and is declared without the arm (Q2 = B).** The code passes every check below. Line numbers are at the head above.

### ① Derived judgments (the eight checks)

1. **Self-host unchanged: PASS.** `registerAuthRoutes` keeps the `getRawApp` probe and calls `mountAuthRoutes(rawApp, ctx, 'host')` (`auth-plugin.ts:3747-3760`) from the same `kernel:ready` point (`:1593`). The sequence of the 55 `rawApp.use/get/post/on/all(` calls in `mountAuthRoutes` is identical, line for line, to `registerAuthRoutes` on `origin/main` (extracted and diffed). `table` is read in four places only: the hand-off's `server` (`:5136`), the catch-all's rethrow (`:5738`), root discovery (`:5783`) and the start-up line (`:5789`); on `'host'` each takes the previous branch. The host catch-all calls `handleVendorRequest` (`:5661`), the previous body, so the middlewares run once (pinned by `isClientIpAllowed` called once on the host mount and once through `handleRequest`).
2. **Nothing reachable through `handleRequest` that self-host does not serve: PASS.** One function fills both tables (`:3760`, `:3783`). The body holds no registration that depends on run-time state: its only conditionals are `typeof rawApp.use === 'function'` and the two `table === 'host'` ones, and it assigns no field, hook, service or timer. The private table drops only `registerOidcDiscoveryRoutes`.
3. **Errors: PASS.** Private catch-all rethrows (`:5738`); the table's `onError` rethrows (`:3780-3782`); `fetch` is `async`, so a synchronous throw is a rejection (`:3788-3789`). The 30 `INTERNAL_ERROR` catches, `/config` (`:3934-3935`, log line added) and the host catch-all answer `INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE` and log. No `err.message` remains in a route catch of `auth-plugin.ts`; `:4477` relays a declared API-key lifecycle refusal, which is the caller's answer, not a fault. Self-host 500 bodies: acceptable. Codes (`INTERNAL_ERROR`, `AUTH_CONFIG_ERROR`, both in `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`), statuses and envelope shapes are unchanged; the text of a 5xx is not a published accept set, and `packages/types/src/error-leak.ts` already states the boundary rule (generic text to the client, full text to the log). A security item is with the owner seat.
4. **Transport peer: PASS.** `handleRequest` hands `transport` to the table (`auth-manager.ts:4091`); it rides the env under a module-private symbol (`auth-plugin.ts:486`, `:3789`), which `readTransportPeerAddress` reads first (`:524-528`). The hono embed passes `c.env.incoming`'s peer (`adapters/hono/src/index.ts:1043-1044`); the runtime `/auth` domain passes `context.request.remoteAddress` (`runtime/src/domains/auth.ts:144-149`). No bound table, or a path outside `basePath`, goes to `handleVendorRequest` (`auth-manager.ts:4091-4092`). `ownsRoute` matches `METHOD path` with HEAD as GET (`auth-plugin.ts:3784-3792`, `auth-manager.ts:4387-4399`); exact-path matching is complete because the table registers no parameterised route.
5. **Re-dispatch: PASS.** All six use the vendor entry: catch-all (`auth-plugin.ts:5661`), `handleWithTransportOf` (`:4153`), `admin/remove-user` (`:4879`), `admin/has-permission` (`:4956`), `sys-session-revoke.ts:211`, `runSsoCallback`'s start (`auth-manager.ts:4220`). No other non-test `handleRequest(` call remains in `plugin-auth/src` (grep). The catch-all asks `ownsVendorRoute` (`:5676`).
6. **Contract surface: PASS on shape, FAIL on the declaration.** `IAuthService.handleRequest(request: Request)` is unchanged; three jsdoc lines, one sentence (`auth-service.ts:164-167`). `OneTimeTokenHandoffServing.server` is exported from the package root (`index.ts:52`), so accepting `null` is a widening of a published type: `Clause-②: yes` stands on that alone, as it does on the new public `AuthManager.handleVendorRequest` / `ownsVendorRoute` / `bindRouteSurface` and on `ownsRoute` answering `true` for more routes. The arm is the defect: see ③.
7. **Tests: PASS.** (i) filters `AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER` on `source === 'objectstack'` and runs `it.each` over the result, with a per-row control that better-auth alone answers its disclaiming 404; a row added later is covered with no edit. A route missing from the private table falls to the catch-all and equals the disclaimer, so the reported ablation legs (42 red; 1 red) follow from the test's structure. Read, not re-run. (ii) compares the two tables' `routes` in order, minus `/.well-known/`, and asserts every private route sits under the base. Allow-list: by handed peer, no peer refused, `trustProxy` + XFF outside the ranges 403 `IP_NOT_ALLOWED`, `/config` exempt. Rejection (async and sync), fallbacks, recursion (one `handleRequest` call on two bridges) and the hand-off 401/302 pair are each pinned.
8. **No secret echo; wording: PASS.** The fixtures are the suite's usual test secret and RFC 5737 addresses. Commits, changeset and PR body state rules. Nit N1 below.

### ② Semver level (Q1)

**Q1 = A, confirmed: `patch` on all four packages.** AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: "The level follows the kind alone … `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (`:12-13`, `:909-910`, `:924-927`) refuses any `minor` beside a declared `none`. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: nothing a metadata author writes changed. The card's "`minor` changeset" loses to the rule. The level stays `patch` after the must-fix.

### ③ Boundary flags (Q2)

**Q2 = B: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is owed.** Requests a published entry answered before are refused after:

- `AuthManager.handleRequest(request)` called with no transport, on a deployment with allowed IP ranges set and no trusted proxy, is refused 403 `IP_NOT_ALLOWED` (the PR's own test pins it: "No peer and no trusted header … refused"). The runtime `/auth` domain does the same for a Fetch `Request`, which carries no `remoteAddress`.
- The one-account rule, the organization IP list and the platform-admin wrappers on the vendor's admin paths now judge requests the forward used to hand to the vendor alone.

The repo's precedent is on the same setting in the same package: `.changeset/30203-allowed-ip-ranges-live.md` and `.changeset/30312-auth-settings-clear-applies-default.md` declare `yes (narrowing)` with a BREAKING banner for one save that is newly refused. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs:914-919` names "a narrowing (a driver, a posture)" as the arm's case and keeps its banner and disposition at `patch`. That the checks are self-host's existing behaviour, and that cloud's rollout is gated in cloud#4384, does not cover an embedder outside this org, who learns it only from the changeset.

### ④ Design judgment

`auth-service.ts`: the added sentence holds against the code (`auth-manager.ts:4089-4093` plus the bound table) and against ADR-0090 D10. One registration function for both tables is the right mechanism: the equality the card asks for is structural, and tests (i)/(ii) pin it.

### Must-fix (FAIL until done; the delta is the declaration faces only)

1. PR body and changeset: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with its reason (and the card's claim line to match).
2. Changeset body: a **BREAKING** banner that says who moves and the one-line fix: a host forwarding to `auth.handleRequest` passes `{ remoteAddress }` as the second argument, or declares `server.trustProxy` behind a proxy. Exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker.
3. PR body: the `Skills-docs:` line the arm owes, and the dogfood battery the arm owes (the report marks it n/a for lack of the arm).

### Nits (accepted or follow-up)

- N1. PR body, "Acceptance notes", second bullet: say only that a security item is with the owner seat.
- N2. Not measured: on self-host, a 404 the host catch-all yields that a dispatcher `/auth` route then forwards to `handleRequest` runs the mount-layer middlewares a second time on the private table (before, it re-ran the vendor alone).
- N3. `bindRouteSurface` is public and marked `@internal`; a caller can unbind the table. Accepted as wiring.

CI at this head when read: 25 success, 9 skipped, 31 in progress, 0 failed (`Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards` green).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-32637-auth-handlerequest-surface`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Q4EjjPP1zuWBNq3nBXVei9`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Head-sha: `85b1f22905a7d211297eafa55671d98c65be13a5`
Delta-from: a517fa2e18 (comment 6821970452)
Verdict: PASS

Delta review. The previous verdict failed on the declaration only; this one re-reads the declaration and confirms nothing else moved. No blocking item.

1. **Delta confirmed, changeset only.** `git diff a517fa2e18..85b1f22905` is one commit, one file: `.changeset/auth-handlerequest-whole-surface.md` (+11 / -3). No source, test, lockfile or doc file moved, so the eight code checks of the previous review stand unchanged. Whole PR against the merge base `c4b6160d21`: 23 files, +921 / -106.

2. **Changeset: correct.**
   - Level: all four entries (`plugin-auth`, `hono`, `runtime`, `spec`) stay `patch`, as `Metadata-protocol: none` requires (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3).
   - `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is present and line-initial. Its reason matches the code: `AuthManager.handleRequest` sends a request under `basePath` to the bound table (`auth-manager.ts:4089`), whose first middleware is the allow-list (`auth-plugin.ts`, `rawApp.use(basePath/*)`), and `isClientIpAllowed` refuses an undetermined address while ranges are set. The widening sentence (new `AuthManager` members, `OneTimeTokenHandoffServing.server` accepting `null`) is accurate too.
   - `Metadata-protocol: none`: present; no authorable key, value or type changes.
   - **BREAKING** banner: names who moves (the forwarding host) and the fix. I checked the fix against the trust rule (`client-address.ts` `resolveClientAddress`: `forwarded ?? remoteAddress`, forwarded headers read only under `trustProxy`). On the private table the peer is read from the transport handed to `handleRequest` and from nothing else (`readTransportPeerAddress`, the `AUTH_SURFACE_TRANSPORT` binding). So `handleRequest(request, { remoteAddress })` establishes the address, and so does `server.trustProxy` with an `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Real-IP` header. Either is sufficient to end the "address cannot be established" refusal. The claim that the `@objectstack/hono` embed and the dispatcher's `/auth` domain already pass the peer is true (`packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts:1043-1044`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/auth.ts:146-149`).
   - ADR-0087: exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with a reason. Same category and same form as the precedent `.changeset/30203-allowed-ip-ranges-live.md`.
   - Summary line `feat(plugin-auth)!:` is accepted: the ADR-0087 gate reads it as the `bang` signal.
   - Against the precedent: same structure throughout (bang summary, `yes (narrowing)` with reason, `none`, `Skills-docs`, one marker, banner, a "Who moves" bullet).
   - Gates run locally at this head, in a scratch worktree, merge base `c4b6160d21`:
     - `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main --event <this PR's payload>`: exit 0. No `major`; level axis green, `yes (narrowing)` with `none` at `patch`.
     - `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main`: exit 0. One declared-breaking changeset, signals `BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing`, disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
   - Nit, non-blocking: the "Who moves" bullet gives the fix for the address case only. The other checks a forwarding host now runs (one account per request, the organization IP list, the platform-admin wrappers) are named in the banner and have no host-side fix, since they are the intended enforcement. One clause saying so would help a reader of the CHANGELOG.

3. **PR body: agrees with the changeset.**
   - `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx` are all present and line-initial. Value and arm match the changeset; the `Skills-docs` line is word for word the same. The body's Clause-② reason omits the changeset's last sentence (the widening list), which is a difference of length and not of claim.
   - The `Skills-docs` claim is true: that page's `handleRequest` section still shows the one-argument call and says nothing of the mount-layer checks, and no file under `skills/**` mentions `handleRequest`, `allowed_ip_ranges` or `trustProxy`.
   - Seat step, not a dev item: `follow-up owed — FILES` is to be rewritten to `follow-up #N` once the card is filed, before acceptance.
   - Title without `!`: **nit, non-blocking.** No gate and no rule requires it. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` read the changeset body and the PR body, never the title; `pr-body-guards.yml` has no title check; AGENTS.md's only title rule is the model-identifier ban. Recommended all the same: the title becomes the squash subject on `main`, and breaking PRs there carry the bang by convention (28 of the last 400 subjects).

4. **Check-runs at 85b1f22905: 72 total, 61 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending.** No red. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are green (each ran twice, once per body edit). The PR reads `mergeable_state: clean`.

5. **N2 (a disclaimed 404 runs the private table twice in the `@objectstack/hono` embed): acceptable here, non-blocking.** Judged by reading, not re-measured. The embed calls `handleRequest`, gets a 404 that `ownsRoute` disclaims, yields, and the adapter's own `${prefix}/*` dispatcher catch-all forwards the same request to `handleRequest` again. Before this PR the same path ran better-auth twice, so the shape is not new; what is new is that the mount-layer middlewares run on both passes. That costs time and nothing else: a second pass happens only after the first one admitted the request, so a refusal (403) is never doubled and no refusal is audited twice, and a disclaimed path reaches no state-changing route. Worth a follow-up card to give the embed one pass per request; it does not belong in this PR.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`auth.handleRequest` 改为在每个内核的一张私有路由表上回答登录插件的全部接口（框架自挂的 42 条加 better-auth 全部），自托管仍在原调用点、按原顺序挂同一批路由。
- 为什么改：托管等宿主把登录请求转给 `handleRequest` 时，以前只到 better-auth，框架自挂接口一律 404，cloud 只能逐条照抄；现在宿主不改代码就拿到全部接口和同样的挂载层检查（维护者裁决「同意 S1」）。
- 风险与回滚：这是一次收窄（`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`）。转发方开始执行 IP 白名单等挂载层检查，设了 `allowed_ip_ranges` 却没传客户端地址、也没声明可信代理的请求会得到 403。托管侧由 cloud#4384 在升级钉版前先测量影响；回滚即回退本 PR，接口形状不变。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts`、`auth-manager.ts`、`auth-handle-request-surface.test.ts`，以及 changeset 的 BREAKING 横幅。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/auth-handle-request-surface.test.ts`，预期 62 passed。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

席位意见：代码两轮契约复审都通过，申报已补齐，合并主干后 PR 自身的 diff 逐字节不变，全部检查绿，落地。

## 席位核对

Verdict: **ACCEPT** · head `06bca6c551` · card objectstack#32637 (claim amended to `Clause-②: yes` with the narrowing arm)

- **Form:** draft, base `main`, `Fixes #32637`. Title `feat(plugin-auth)!:`. Body lines `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Skills-docs: follow-up #32725`. 23 files, +921 −106 (1027 lines, under 3000). No governed path (read from the files list). It touches `packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts` (4 lines), so the path limb holds as well as the declaration limb.
- **Contract review:** round 1 at comment 6821970452 (a517fa2e). The code passed all eight checks; the declaration was FAIL. The delta review at comment 6823508864 (85b1f22905) is **PASS**. The head then moved only by merging origin/main (06bca6c551, no conflicts). The dev measured the three-dot PR diff as byte-identical before and after the merge (same 23 files, sha256 equal), so the PASS covers the current diff.
- **Gates:** `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` exit 0 (the reviewer reproduced both). `dispatch-gates` at 06bca6c551: 108/108 families run, 0 unmeasured. Check-runs at 06bca6c551: 59 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed, and every required context is green, including Dogfood Regression Gate and Test Core 8/8. The narrowing dogfood battery ran locally at 85b1f22905 (3798 passed). K=3.
- **Accepted deviations:** the PR-body signature trailer, which the relay requires.
- **Out of scope:**
  - Skills-docs → filed objectstack#32725.
  - N2 (the `@objectstack/hono` embed runs the private table twice for a 404 no route serves) → `dropped`. It costs time only, on a path no route serves; better-auth already ran twice there before this PR; nothing pulls on it.
  - The round-1 private security item stays with its owner seat.
  - Reviewer nit: the "Who moves" bullet gives a host-side fix only for the address case → Acceptance notes.
- **Landing:** `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay, in the same stroke as this comment. Hosted adoption waits on cloud#4384's measurement before the pin moves.
